items.text: I try new ways of doing things at work.
I prefer work that requires original thinking.
When something does not function well at work, I try to find a new solution.
I try to get new ideas from colleagues, schools or partners.
I am interested in how things are done elsewhere in order to use those ideas in my own work.
I search for other people’s new ideas in order to try to implement the best ones.
When I have a new idea, I try to persuade my colleagues of it.
When I have a new idea, I try to get support for it from my manager or leadership.
I try to show my colleagues the positive sides of new ideas.
When I have a new idea, I try to involve people who are able to collaborate on it.
I develop suitable plans and schedules for the implementation of new ideas.
I look for and secure the resources or budget needed to implement new ideas.
To implement new ideas, I search for new tools, processes or procedures.
When problems occur during implementation, I get them into the hands of those who can solve them.
I try to involve key decision makers in the implementation of an idea.
When I have a new idea, I look for people who are able to push it through.
I am able to persistently overcome obstacles when implementing an idea.
I do not give up even when others say it cannot be done.
I usually do not finish until I accomplish the goal.
During idea implementation, I am able to persist even when work is not going well at the moment.
I have often been successful at work in implementing my ideas and putting them into practice.
Many things I came up with are used in the IB.
Wherever I have worked, I improved something there.
My manager motivates me to come to them with new ideas.
My manager makes sure good ideas are recognised.
My manager supports me in implementing good ideas as soon as possible.
My manager is tolerant of mistakes and errors during the implementation of something new.
My manager is able to obtain support for my proposals outside our department.
The way people are recognised in the IB motivates them to suggest new things and procedures.
The IB has set aside sufficient resources to support the implementation of new ideas.
The IB provides people with time for putting ideas and innovations into practice.
I develop new ideas together with the people who will use them.
I change my ideas in response to feedback from the people they affect.
I test ideas with others before I am sure they will work.
In my team, people put forward views that go against the majority.
In my team, we argue about ideas without it becoming personal.
In my team, we hear an idea out before judging it.
In my team, we try small versions of ideas before planning them in full.
In my team, we change course when something we tried does not work.
In my team, we learn more from what we build than from what we discuss.
When my team disagrees, we look for an option that takes something from each side.
In my team, decisions are made without one person’s view simply winning.
My team can agree a way forward while people still disagree.
